content:
Every year, Apple launches the "Back to School" promotion for students. During the promotional period, purchasing a Mac or iPad comes with special rewards. In the past, these have typically been offered in the form of free gifts (such as AirPods) or Apple gift cards valued between US$100 and US$150. According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, the promotion will return later this week.

The promotion should have already kicked off, but Apple has been forced to delay its launch due to significant price hikes caused by a memory shortage.

However, Gurman noted that Apple is reportedly set to put up promotional materials in retail stores by "mid-week," meaning the promotion could officially launch as early as within this week.

It remains unknown whether this year's offer will be more attractive than in previous years. Given the substantial price increases on Mac and iPad, Apple may further enhance the promotion to ease the financial burden on students.

Another point worth mentioning is that Apple recently added UNiDAYS verification to its US education store. Going forward, only verified students will be eligible for the related offers.

As for what Apple has in store this time, we'll have to wait and see. Hopefully, despite the sharp price increases, the promotion will still be enticing enough for students to make a purchase.
